subject: Culture
title: Green Burials
description: A micro-lesson that makes Green Burials usable.

hook.text: A company in Washington state turns human remains into soil in 30 days. Your body becomes a garden.

buildup.text: Traditional US burials use 4.3 million gallons of embalming fluid and 20 million board feet of hardwood annually.

discovery.text: Green burials skip embalming, use biodegradable shrouds, and let the body decompose naturally into the earth.

twist.text: Jewish and Muslim burials have always been green—plain shroud, no embalming, buried quickly in contact with soil.

climax.text: Human composting is now legal in several US states. The death industry faces its first disruption in a century.

punchline.text: The greenest funeral is also the oldest one.

quiz.question: How long does human composting take?
